solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Cricket and telly where there could be culture? (4,4)

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match

annotation.surface: An evening of cricket on the telly, sneered at as the opposite of culture.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface sets sport and TV against high culture; the definition means a bacterial culture, grown in a lab. The question mark flags that playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Laboratory cultures of bacteria are grown in test tubes.

entries.clue: Stew not yet cooked? (2-2)

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be agitated; the noun sense is a fuss or commotion
a dish not yet cooked is still on the list of jobs; the question mark flags a phrase read literally

annotation.surface: A cook eyeing a pot of stew that is still raw.
annotation.walkthrough: Both halves pretend to be about cooking. A to-do is a fuss, which is what a stew is; and a dish not yet cooked is still to do.
annotation.definitionFit: A to-do is a commotion or fuss, just as a stew is.

entries.clue: Petition on that basis allowed (7)

annotation.surface: A petition accepted because it meets the rules.
annotation.definitionFit: To petition someone is to solicit, to ask earnestly.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Petition' looks like a noun in the surface but is the verb, to ask formally; LICIT is the less familiar root of illicit.

entries.clue: Clear up right after a bit of carpentry (5)

blocks.note: net = clear, as in net profit; 'up' turns it over in a down clue
on = right, acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

annotation.surface: Tidying up the workshop properly once some carpentry is done.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clear up' reads as tidying, but it splits: 'Clear' is the net of net profit, and 'up' tells you to read it upwards in this down entry.
annotation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue on a piece of wood that fits into a mortise joint.

indicatorNotes.up: in a down entry, up means read from the bottom, so the word is turned over
indicatorNotes.after: coming after means placed later in the answer

entries.clue: Book and at least three gardening tools fitting inside drum (5,4)

blocks.note: RAKES (at least two) + HOE (one more) makes three or more tools

annotation.surface: A gardener's shopping list: a book and a few tools.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At least three' is the setter's joke: rakes are plural, so two or more, and the hoe makes at least three. The 'drum' is a brake drum on a car wheel.
annotation.definitionFit: A brake shoe is the curved part that presses outward inside the brake drum.

entries.clue: Soviet region’s terminal east of Russian river (6)

blocks.note: the Ob is a great Siberian river

annotation.surface: Directions to a railway terminus in some far corner of the old USSR.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terminal' pretends to be a railway station in the surface; it is the adjective meaning final. Across entries run west to east.
annotation.definitionFit: An oblast is an administrative region of the Soviet Union and of Russia today.

indicatorNotes.east of: on a map east is to the right, and in an across entry to the right means later

entries.clue: For one throwing away clothes, where to start? (9)

annotation.definition: For one throwing away clothes, where to start?

blocks.note: a stripper, whose act ends with no clothes on
read as 'wear to start': the only point of the act when clothes are worn

annotation.surface: Someone clearing out a wardrobe, wondering where to start.
annotation.walkthrough: Read 'where to start' as 'wear to start': a stripper's clothes are worn only at the beginning. Straight, 'where to start' simply means the beginning.
annotation.definitionFit: The beginning is where you start; for a stripper, the clothes belong only to the beginning.

entries.clue: Stress back home upset Sue on vacation (7)

blocks.note: ten years back = ten years ago
at home = in; 'upset' turns it up in a down clue
SUE emptied of its middle leaves S…E

annotation.surface: A woman's trip away unsettles the household left behind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' means emptied: a vacated word keeps only its outside letters. 'Back' is not a reversal here; it means ago.
annotation.definitionFit: Stress as a verb, to worry anxiously, is a plain synonym of agonise.

indicatorNotes.upset: something upset is turned over, and in a down entry that means read upwards
indicatorNotes.on vacation: a vacated place is emptied, so the word keeps only its outside letters

entries.clue: Not being late by skirting queues? (10)

blocks.note: three by four = three times four

annotation.surface: Someone who dodges the queues so as never to be late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like a link word but is the multiplication sign, as in three by four. Queues are called lines in American English.
annotation.definitionFit: Timeliness names the quality; 'not being late' is a negative paraphrase of it.

indicatorNotes.skirting: a skirt goes round the outside, so one word wraps round the other

entries.clue: List that could be read in three parts for us (4)

blocks.note: us is the speaker plus the listener, joined by a clipped 'and'

annotation.surface: A list someone hopes we can decode together.
annotation.walkthrough: Say the answer as three words, me 'n' you, and together they make us.
annotation.definitionFit: A restaurant's bill of fare is a list, and so is a computer's list of options.
indicators: could be read in three parts

indicatorNotes.could be read in three parts: the answer spoken as three separate words gives another phrase

entries.clue: Trace source of unusual food eaten when cycling (9)

blocks.note: a deli sells unusual imported food
EATEN with its last letter moved round to the front

annotation.surface: Tracking down where some odd dish came from after eating it on a bike ride.
annotation.walkthrough: 'When cycling' means the letters rotate: the N at the end of EATEN comes round to the start.
annotation.definitionFit: To trace an outline and to delineate both mean to draw or describe precisely.

indicatorNotes.when cycling: cycling letters travel round, the last one coming back to the front

entries.clue: Prepare for role in good play (5)

blocks.note: play = room to move, as in play in a rope

annotation.surface: An actor getting ready for a part in a fine production.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' pretends to be a drama, but it is slack or free movement, so ROOM.
annotation.definitionFit: To groom someone is to prepare them for a particular role, such as a successor.

entries.clue: Weighty arguments against peer eating beans this regularly (13)

annotation.surface: A long case against a lord who eats beans every day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peer' suggests the House of Lords, but here it means an equal, as in tried by one's peers.
annotation.definitionFit: Weighty in the figurative sense, having important results, is what consequential means.

indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten ends up inside, so one chunk goes into another
indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so every other letter

entries.clue: Trump heard Republican skewering silly crude text (5,5)

blocks.note: to ruff is to trump in card games
daft = silly; R goes through it

annotation.surface: A politician's garbled, rude message, read aloud.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trump' tempts you to the president, which the Republican keeps alive, but it is the card-game verb: to ruff is to play a trump.
annotation.definitionFit: A rough draft is an unpolished first version of a text.

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling
indicatorNotes.skewering: a skewer runs through meat, so one chunk goes through the middle of another

entries.clue: Performing dance with specialist shoes easy to access (2,3)

blocks.note: an actor who is on is performing
tap dancers wear shoes with metal plates

annotation.surface: A tap dancer's shoes being handy for the show.
annotation.definitionFit: Something on tap is readily available, like beer from a barrel.
annotation.walkthrough: A tap dancer's shoes have metal plates on the soles. The phrase is borrowed from beer drawn straight from the barrel.

entries.clue: PTA in real knots dealing with end of term and after (9)

annotation.definition: dealing with end of term and after
annotation.surface: A parent-teacher association tied up in knots over the end of the school term.
annotation.walkthrough: The school surface makes 'term' a school term; here it is the term of a pregnancy, and 'after' is just after birth.
annotation.definitionFit: Perinatal describes the period around birth, from late pregnancy to just after delivery.

indicatorNotes.knots: something in knots is tangled, so the letters are jumbled

entries.clue: Fellow British annoy an insular Scot (9)

blocks.note: to ride someone is to needle or annoy them

annotation.surface: A Briton needling a standoffish Scotsman.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Insular' reads as narrow-minded, but here means living on islands: the Hebrides lie off Scotland's west coast.
annotation.definitionFit: Insular in its literal sense means of an island, so an insular Scot is an islander from the Hebrides.

entries.clue: Shower leaving dirty marks? Not so bad taking bath (9)

blocks.note: a spa is a place to bathe; SPA goes inside BETTER

annotation.surface: A grimy shower, and a bath being the cleaner option.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shower' is a verb here, to shower someone with muck, not the thing in the bathroom.
annotation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to splash with dirt, a shower that leaves marks.

indicatorNotes.taking: to take in is to hold inside, so one word goes into another

entries.clue: Head girl has recovered from being in love with head teacher (9)

blocks.note: a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness

annotation.surface: A school's head girl getting over a crush on the head teacher.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head girl' reads as a school title, but it only gives G. The second 'head' is a promontory, NESS, as in Dungeness on the English coast.
annotation.definitionFit: A governess is a private teacher employed in a family's home.

indicatorNotes.Head: the head of a word is its first letter

entries.clue: Scat by large deer — one dropping from that (7)

annotation.surface: Droppings found beside a big deer, with 'scat' in its tracker's sense.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scat' looks like a noun, animal dung, which the deer and 'dropping' support; it is the verb meaning clear off.
annotation.definitionFit: Scat! and Vamoose! both mean go away quickly.

indicatorNotes.dropping from: something dropping from a word leaves it, so that letter is removed

entries.clue: Like wearing doctor’s pants (5)

blocks.note: a GP is a family doctor

annotation.surface: Someone dressing up in a doctor's underpants.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British for underpants in the surface, but it is the verb: breathes hard. A GP is a general practitioner, the family doctor.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who gasps pants for breath.

indicatorNotes.wearing: one word wears the other like a coat, wrapped round it

entries.clue: Saudi travelling around noon left face partly shaded (7)

annotation.surface: A Saudi traveller at midday whose face is half in shade.
annotation.walkthrough: The face belongs to the sundial, not the traveller: the gnomon casts a shadow across part of the dial.
annotation.definitionFit: A sundial's face always has a shadow across part of it.

indicatorNotes.travelling: letters on the move rearrange themselves
indicatorNotes.around: the letters are spread around the others, all mixed together

entries.clue: Show wizard standing astride river (13)

blocks.note: a demon at something is a wizard at it

annotation.surface: A magician's act on a bridge over a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wizard' means an expert, and so does demon, as in a demon bowler.
annotation.definitionFit: A demonstration is a show of how something works.

indicatorNotes.astride: standing astride means one leg either side, so one word goes round the other

entries.clue: Place with parts not built up (4)

blocks.note: 'built up' turns it upwards in a down clue; W parts TO…N

annotation.surface: Somewhere with patches still undeveloped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Not built up' reads as undeveloped, an ironic hint since a town is a built-up area; really 'built up' turns NOT over.
annotation.definitionFit: Place is a general word for a settlement, and a town is one kind; the clue's ironic 'not built up' hints at the opposite.

indicatorNotes.parts: to part something is to split it, so W sits in the middle of another word
indicatorNotes.built up: in a down entry building up means going upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

entries.clue: Dress for pilgrimage in India, hot being covered with fleece (5)

blocks.note: I = India in the NATO alphabet
a ram is a creature covered with fleece

annotation.surface: Pilgrim's clothing in India, too hot with woollen layers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Being' is a noun: the creature covered with fleece is a RAM. The ihram is the plain white garment worn by Muslim pilgrims to Mecca.
annotation.definitionFit: The ihram is the dress worn by pilgrims on the hajj.

entries.clue: Melted part bubbled up, you’d say (4)

blocks.note: water welled up from the spring

annotation.surface: Something molten bubbling to the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A weld is the joint where metal parts have been melted together.

indicatorNotes.you’d say: what you would say is spoken, so the sound counts, not the spelling

annotation.walkthrough: Melted here describes the joint itself: 'Melted part' is a noun phrase, a part joined by melting.

entries.clue: Going on further than intended, almost back (5)

blocks.note: TOO FAR, 'almost' drops its last letter

annotation.surface: Walking on past where you meant to stop, then almost turning back.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'going on' a walk that went too far; it is the definition, as in 'something is afoot'.
annotation.definitionFit: Afoot originally meant on foot and moving, hence 'going on', happening.

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes
indicatorNotes.back: going back means reversing the direction of reading

entries.clue: Littoral reshaped by delta, as it were (9)

blocks.note: D = delta in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A coastline remodelled by a river delta, so to speak.
annotation.walkthrough: 'As it were' looks like a hedge but is fodder; 'delta' pretends to be the river mouth, which fits the coastal scene, but is just D.
annotation.definitionFit: Littoral means the shore, the land at the waterside.

indicatorNotes.reshaped: something reshaped has the same material in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

entries.clue: Young chorister leaving out quaver in the middle (6)

blocks.note: to quaver is to tremble; its middle letter M goes

annotation.surface: A choirboy whose voice has stopped wobbling mid-note.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Quaver' suggests a musical note in the choir scene, but it is the verb, to tremble; TREMBLE loses its central M.
annotation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy singing the highest part in a choir.

indicatorNotes.leaving out: leaving out means omitting, so letters are removed
indicatorNotes.in the middle: points to the central letter of the word

entries.clue: Unusual parking light on front of car folded up (8)

annotation.surface: An odd parking light on a car's bumper after a shunt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Front of car' supplies C, and 'on' puts it at the start. The folded-up car in the surface is exactly what crumpled describes.
annotation.definitionFit: Folded up describes something crushed into creases, the literal sense of crumpled.

indicatorNotes.on: placed on means placed before in an across entry
indicatorNotes.front of: the front of a word is its first letter
